title: Transformer-Based Time-Series Inference of Lindblad Dynamics in Open Quantum Systems
abstract: The Lindblad master equation is the standard framework for describing the non-unitary evolution of open quantum systems, where environmental interactions induce dissipation and decoherence. When both the system Hamiltonian and the dissipation rates are partially unknown or explicitly time-dependent, traditional analytical inversion and system-identification techniques become intractable. Recent works have demonstrated that Transformer-based models can infer unknown dissipation rates from observable time series, yet these approaches typically rely on hand-crafted statistical features under idealized and highly restricted conditions. Here we advance the paradigm by introducing a raw time-series Transformer that directly ingests the full trajectories of Pauli expectation values $\langleσ_x(t)\rangle$, $\langleσ_y(t)\rangle$, and $\langleσ_z(t)\rangle$, thereby fully exploiting the self-attention mechanism for temporal modeling. The architecture is further extended to jointly learn unknown Hamiltonian parameters, handle multiple dissipation channels, and operate robustly under realistic measurement noise. Across all tested scenarios the model achieves consistently high reconstruction accuracy while eliminating manual feature engineering. This provides a scalable, robust, and versatile framework for quantum environment sensing in realistic open quantum systems.
summary: This paper introduces a novel Transformer-based framework to solve the inverse problem of open quantum system dynamics. By directly processing raw time-series data of Pauli expectation values, the model can robustly and automatically infer unknown, time-dependent dissipation rates and Hamiltonian parameters. This represents a significant advancement over prior machine learning methods that required manual feature engineering.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenging inverse problem of inferring unknown or time-dependent dissipation rates and Hamiltonian parameters in open quantum systems when traditional analytical methods fail.
main_result: A raw time-series Transformer model was developed that achieves high reconstruction accuracy for unknown parameters by directly ingesting raw Pauli expectation value trajectories, eliminating the need for manual feature engineering.
method: The authors employ an encoder-only Transformer architecture, using self-attention to process the full time-series data of Pauli expectation values ($\langle\sigma_i(t)angle$) to jointly learn unknown system parameters.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum system governed by the Lindblad master equation. The dynamics are characterized by a Hamiltonian $H$ and time-dependent dissipation channels $\gamma_k(t)$.
key_observables: Expectation values of Pauli operators ($\langle\sigma_x(t)angle, \langle\sigma_y(t)angle, \langle\sigma_z(t)angle$).
important_parameters: Time-dependent dissipation rates $\gamma_k(t)$, unknown Hamiltonian parameters (e.g., $h$), and the coefficients defining the parameterization (e.g., Bernstein polynomial coefficients).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are modeled using the Born-Markov approximation, and the model assumes the system can be parameterized by a known functional form (e.g., Bernstein or sinusoidal) for the unknown rates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the raw time-series analysis for single-qubit dissipation using Bernstein polynomials, the joint inference of unknown Hamiltonian parameters alongside dissipation, and the robustness of the method under varying levels of measurement and preparation noise.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure covering background theory (Lindblad equation, Transformer basics), detailed methodology (raw time-series Transformer implementation), and comprehensive evaluation results demonstrating performance across various noise and parameter regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, data-driven tool for characterizing complex quantum environments by bypassing the need for restrictive analytical assumptions, making it highly relevant for experimental quantum optics and open quantum system research.
